header: Date: 2026-03-07 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Redwood AE+SE (Avery Chen, Samir Patel), Product (Lina Morales), NovaEdge (Elena Ruiz, Marcus Lee, Priya Singh, Tom Baxter)
summary: Technical sync between Redwood and NovaEdge to align on marketplace listing, reference architecture for joint solution, and next steps for pilot and submission. Key topics: listing requirements, reference deploy pattern (VPC, peering, private endpoints), SSO/KMS/audit logs, billing & marketplace pricing model, joint marketing assets, and timeline for pilot and submission.
topics: Reference architecture for joint deployment (VPC, peering, private endpoints)
Joint solution value props and billing model
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super excited to sync on the NovaEdge joint solution and marketplace listing. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Elena Ruiz: Elena here, hi all.
[00:10] Marcus Lee: Marcus - cloud architect.
[00:12] Priya Singh: Priya, security.
[00:14] Tom Baxter: Tom, PM for marketplace.
[00:17] Samir Patel: Samir from SE, hey.
[00:18] Lina Morales: Lina product.
[00:20] Devon Park: Devon.
[00:25] Avery: Alright so agenda, we wanna cover listing checklist, the reference arch we're proposing, security and SSO, and pilot perf. Also timelines. If any other item shout now.
[00:36] Tom: One ask — can we get sample screenshots and terraform snippets for the listing so I can pre-fill the marketplace UI?
[00:42] Avery: Yup we'll share an example listing and the metadata template. Samir, can you take on terraform snippets?
[00:47] Samir: Yep I’ll pull a couple of examples — suggest we show both hosted and private deployment snippets, and a simple dedicated capacity example.
[00:55] Marcus: That'd be great. On the network side we need clarity on VPC peering vs private endpoint approach. Our security team prefers private endpoints.
[01:03] Samir: Totally. For Redwood private deployments we support customer-managed VPC endpoints and on-prem connectors. The reference arch we propose has two patterns: 1) Marketplace-hosted listing that spins up a managed stack with private endpoint back to NovaEdge VPC, 2) Joint reference where customers deploy NovaEdge + Redwood sidecar within their VPC (private deployment).
[01:27] Priya: Ok quick security check — we need to see SOC2 reports, key management details (KMS/HSM support), and audit logging retention. Also SSO: we use SAML 2.0 via IdP and want SCIM for provisioning.
[01:41] Lina: We have SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts we can share. Redwood supports KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private. We can also provide audit log exports to S3 or partner SIEMs. SCIM + SAML are on our roadmap; SAML SSO and SAML provisioning are supported today for enterprise accounts.
[01:58] Priya: When you say customer-managed keys, is that BYOK with HSM? We require HSM-backed KMS for certain regulated customers.
[02:06] Samir: We integrate with major cloud KMS and can support HSM-backed keys; for on-prem we also support an HSM gateway. We'll need to document the workflow for key rotation and any local encryption at rest.
[02:17] Marcus: Network - what's latency like for private endpoint calls vs hosted? We're concerned about conversational use cases with low latency requirements.
[02:25] Samir: In our internal tests, private endpoint within same region adds negligible overhead — usually sub 10ms more than fully-hosted due to TLS handshake. But depends on path; we'll share perf numbers. For tight SLOs we recommend Dedicated reserved capacity in the same region and local KV cache.
[02:42] Elena: On the marketplace listing itself, what are the categories? Tom, anything we should align on?
[02:47] Tom: The marketplace has categories for AI infra, partner solutions, and joint apps. For listing we need a 1‑line, 3‑bullet value props, 2 screenshots, pricing model and contact, plus logos and legal entity. Billing can be through marketplace or direct (we need to choose).
[03:05] Avery: If we route billing through marketplace there's a delay and fees, but it simplifies procurement. Direct-bill gives faster payouts. We should decide with NovaEdge what makes sense for launch customers.
[03:15] Priya: From security procurement perspective marketplace billing is fine as long as contract clauses are standard. We'll confirm with legal.
[03:22] Marcus: For the reference arch, can you share a terraform module that sets up the private endpoint, routing, and a sample LM model config? That would help our templates.
[03:31] Samir: Yep — I'll include a terraform module and a docker-compose example for on-prem proof of concept. Also sample model config with quantization and batching knobs.
[03:40] Devon: We'll also include a recommended defaults doc — like batch size, kv cache TTL, and fallback policies for degraded modes. That helps partners tune cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:51] Elena: For joint solution messaging, we're thinking "Low-latency, secure LLM inference as an integrated NovaEdge + Redwood offering". We want the reference arch to highlight private control plane and auditability.
[04:03] Lina: Nice. We'll craft 3 bullets: 1) enterprise-grade low-latency inference, 2) flexible deployment (hosted/dedicated/private), 3) predictable cost controls and observability.
[04:14] Tom: On assets — we'll need logos (SVG + PNG), short video or GIF, and any sample templates for listing copy.
[04:21] Avery: We'll produce the copy bundle and sample screenshots. Expect that by Tuesday.
[04:27] Priya: For audits — can we get a data flow diagram showing where logs and telemetry go and retention options? We need that for procurement.
[04:35] Samir: I'll draft a dataflow showing request paths, what is logged, where logs are stored, and retention options (30/90/365 days). For partner listings we can include a standard summary and offer extended retention as an add-on.
[04:47] Marcus: Also curious about quotas and rate limiting per tenant for the marketplace deployment — we need to set sensible defaults to avoid noisy neighbor.
[04:55] Samir: We'll suggest rate limit defaults and per-tenant quotas; Dedicated deployments can set much higher caps. Caching/prefix caching will also reduce token costs.
[05:05] Elena: Pilot scope — we propose a 6-week pilot with 3 customers: one hosted marketplace deploy, one private endpoint test, one dedicated capacity smoke test. Does that timeline work?
[05:16] Lara: (note: speaker mislabel) Sorry, I mean Samir, that seems fine, we can scope perf tests and success criteria.
[05:22] Samir: For perf we'll run latency p95, throughput, and token cost baseline. We'll share a spreadsheet with workload configs.
[05:30] Marcus: On legal, any required partner agreement templates? We'll need an MOU for co-marketing and a revenue share outline if we route through marketplace.
[05:38] Avery: Redwood has a partner MOU template. I'll loop in business development and legal and share the draft. For revenue share, we can propose options and let NovaEdge pick.
[05:47] Tom: Operational question: who owns support for marketplace customers? Is it NovaEdge or Redwood?
[05:52] Lina: We usually do tiered support: initial triage via NovaEdge for solution questions, Redwood handles infra/serving incidents. We'll map a runbook for escalation.
[06:03] Priya: SCIM — you mentioned it's roadmap; do you have ETA? Some of our customers require automated provisioning.
[06:09] Samir: SCIM is targeted for Q2 2026 GA; for pilots we can do manual provisioning and script-based automation.
[06:17] Elena: Are we able to include a joint solution tag on Redwood's console and marketplace for co-branding?
[06:22] Avery: Yes we can add partner badges and joint-marketing links. We'll provide the style guide for logos.
[06:29] Tom: One more marketplace nit — we need a short compliance blurb: data residency and where logs are stored. Can Redwood provide that per-region?
[06:36] Samir: Yes, logs and data residency controls are region-aware; we can provide per-region storage and note default retention. We'll include that in the checklist.
[06:44] Priya: For encryption in transit/e2e — is there support for client certificate authentication for private endpoints?
[06:50] Samir: We support mTLS for private endpoints and client cert auth on dedicated/private deploys. We'll include sample cert rotation guidance.
[06:58] Marcus: Great. For the reference arch doc, can you include a diagram of the fallback path if Redwood Dedicated capacity is saturated — like auto-failover to hosted or lower-cost model variant?
[07:08] Samir: Yes we'll detail routing policies: latency-first, cost-first, and fallback to compatible model variants with graceful degradation. Show canary rollouts and health checks.
[07:20] Elena: Ok let's recap next steps. Avery?
[07:24] Avery: Recap: Redwood to send listing checklist, sample screenshots, terraform snippets, dataflow and policy docs by 2026-03-10 to 03-12 window. NovaEdge to send logos, reference arch, and network diagram by 2026-03-14. Pilot kickoff week of 2026-03-23. Follow-up meeting 2026-03-17 to confirm marketplace submission date. Any objections?
[07:44] Tom: Sounds good.
[07:45] Priya: Fine from security side pending artifact review.
[07:48] Marcus: Good.
[07:50] Avery: Alright thanks everyone, we'll send calendar invite for the follow-up.
[07:54] Elena: Thanks all.
[07:56] (call ends)
